title: Word Break
prompt: Given a string `s` and a list of strings `wordDict`, return true if `s` can be segmented into a space-separated sequence of one or more dictionary words. The same word from the dictionary may be reused multiple times in the segmentation.

examples.explanation: "applepenapple" segments as "apple pen apple", reusing "apple" twice.
No combination of dictionary words covers the entire string exactly.

constraints: s and wordDict[i] consist of only lowercase English letters
All the strings of wordDict are unique
hints: Think of dp[i] as: can the prefix s[0:i] be fully segmented into dictionary words?
dp[0] = true (empty prefix trivially segments). For each end position i, check every start position j < i: if dp[j] is true and s[j:i] is in the dictionary, then dp[i] is true.
Convert wordDict to a set first for O(1) membership checks, since you'll be checking substrings repeatedly.

solution.approach: Bottom-up DP where dp[i] means s[0:i] (the first i characters) can be segmented using dictionary words. dp[0] = True as the base case. For each end index i from 1 to len(s), scan every possible split point j from 0 to i-1: if dp[j] is True and the substring s[j:i] exists in the word set, mark dp[i] = True and stop checking further splits for this i. The final answer is dp[len(s)].
solution.timeComplexity: O(n^2) where n = len(s), ignoring substring hashing cost
